description: Semtech Corporation provides semiconductor, Internet of Things systems, and cloud connectivity service solutions in the Asia- Pacific, North America, and Europe. The company operates in three segments
description_full: Semtech Corporation provides semiconductor, Internet of Things systems, and cloud connectivity service solutions in the Asia- Pacific, North America, and Europe. The company operates in three segments: Signal Integrity, Analog Mixed Signal and Wireless, and IoT Systems and Connectivity. It provides signal integrity products, including a portfolio of optical and copper data communications and video transport products used in various infrastructure, and industrial applications; a portfolio of integrated circuits for data centers, enterprise networks, passive optical networks, wireless base station optical transceivers, and interface applications; and video products for broadcast applications, as well as video-over-IP technology for professional audio video applications. The company also offers analog mixed signal and wireless products; protection devices, such as filter and termination devices which protect electronic systems from voltage spikes; and designs, develops, manufactures, and markets radio frequency products used in industrial, medical, and communications applications, as well as specialized sensing products. In addition, it provides switching voltage regulators, combination switching and linear regulators, smart regulators, isolated switches, and wireless charging related products. Further, the company offers a portfolio of IoT systems and connectivity solutions, such as modules, gateways, routers, and connected services, including wireless connectivity and cloud-based services for industrial, medical, and communications applications. It serves original equipment manufacturers, solution providers, commercial applications, infrastructure, high-end consumer, and industrial end markets. The company sells its products through direct sales personnel, independent sales representative firms, and independent distributors. Semtech Corporation was incorporated in 1960 and is headquartered in Camarillo, California.

financial_summary: Semtech Corporation is a mid-cap technology business with a $9.6B market cap on $1.0B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +12% over the past three years and +7% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 5% against a 11% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 59% confirm genuine pricing power.
The business throws off $171M in free cash flow — roughly 16 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
Accruals are elevated at -15.7% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 4.7× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 0.8× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.1× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 3% operating margin is roughly in line with the Technology median (7%).
It captures well under its share of sector profits (0.13x its revenue share).

mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 182% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 32% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 49% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 83% and a beta of 1.39, it amplifies market moves, though its beta has shifted (1y 3.59 vs 5y 1.85), so read it loosely.
Liquidity is deep, with about $438.5M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 51% in the 2020 crash, 71% in the 2022 bear market and 52% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $26.00 (margin of safety -297%), so there is no valuation cushion.
On multiples it looks expensive against Technology peers: P/E 68.4 vs 26.7, EV/EBITDA 49.4 vs 16.4 and P/FCF 56.2 vs 25.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 346% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 1.8% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 0.4% (vs the 8% bar).
The 15 covering analysts target $217 on average, 110% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 5% falls short of the cost of capital of 11.5%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 8.38).
It runs a 59% gross margin and converts 16% of revenue into free cash flow, or 11% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality is mixed: a Piotroski score of 7/9, but cash conversion of only -4.49x and high accruals (-15.7% of assets).
It spends 18.7% of revenue on R&D and 5.5% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is heavy at 4.7x net debt to EBITDA ($195.2M of cash against $491.2M of debt), and interest cover is thin at 0.8x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 7.4, in the safe zone).
Working capital ties up about 136 days of sales, a drag on cash generation.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 11.5% over 3 years, 12.0% over 5 years and 6.8% over 10 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 4.8% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 14.7% a year over five years.
Capex runs only 0.3x depreciation (0.9% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.8%), and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (12 sales, net $3.8M sold).
The share count has grown 7.7% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
people: With about 1,920 employees, each generates about $547K of revenue, 1.5x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 5.4% a year.
That works out to $89K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.6M (3x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (3/10, lower is better).
